newsitem.title: UK: Copper premiums show demand strong - Bankers Trust.
newsitem.headline: Copper premiums show demand strong - Bankers Trust.

text.p: Premiums for physical copper are strong at present and when taken as a global-based average are indicative of solid demand, analysts at Bankers Trust International said.

Taking an average of the physical copper premiums in North America, Europe and the Far East as well as incorporating the shrinking discount for standard cathodes, it is possible to arrive at an aggregate physical premium, Bankers Trust Vice-President Brian Harmon de Clare said.
This overall premium is now well in excess of $50/tonne - the highest since June 1995, he noted.
The premium has climbed from around $36 at a time when London Metal Exchange (LME) prices have been under severe pressure following the shake-out after the Sumitomo Corp scandal.
Prior to June 1996, the relationship between LME prices and the aggregate premium had been consistent. But since then it has diverged with prices falling, but premiums hardening.
"In summary, the very sharp drop in copper prices would have appeared to have stimulated a great deal of physical demand in many areas," Harmon de Clare said.
"Although the market may see occasional arrivals of metal in the warehouses it is unlikely that this influx can be sustained unless these physical premiums drop substantially," he said.
Separately, an analysis of the relationship between LME prices and the overall stocks/weeks consumption ratio also shows a divergence this year.
The ratio is now at 3.8 weeks CRU International data shows, which is the lowest since June 1995.
But whereas cash prices were near $3,000/tonne at that time. They are now at $1,970/tonne, having become de-coupled in the first half of 1996.
